families.title: Shrink strips
families.mathematics: Rows of A and B tiles grow by the substitution A → AB, B → BA, applied to every tile at once; from A they are the prefixes of the Thue–Morse word T, whose tile n (from 0) is A exactly when n has an even number of ones in binary. A piece is a factor of T. Shrinking is desubstitution: seams split a piece into pairs starting at its first or second tile, a tile cut off at an end gets the other letter as its ghost partner, and each pair becomes its first letter; a pair AA or BB is marked. A placement is unmarked with a factor as its shrunk row exactly when the piece occurs in T at a place of that parity, so a piece is a factor exactly when it can shrink, one unmarked placement at a time, to one tile (every word of one or two tiles is a factor, and from three tiles on each shrink is shorter). A non-factor is stuck: every placement, at some level, marks a pair, and the tree of placements is a finite certificate. Factors of four tiles or more have one placement (recognizability); ABA and BAB have two. T has no overlap (Thue 1912), so any repeating strip has a stuck run.
rules: A row grows by turning every A into AB and every B into BA, all at once: A, AB, ABBA, ABBABAAB, and on. A piece is a run of tiles cut from a grown row.

Shrinking undoes one step. Seams split the row into pairs in one of two ways: pair the first two tiles, or leave the first tile alone. A tile cut off from its partner at an end gets the partner back as a dashed ghost, the other letter.
Each pair shrinks to its first letter. A pair AA or BB is marked: no tile grows into it.
A row is stuck when each way of placing its seams marks a pair or shrinks to a stuck row. A row of one or two tiles is never stuck.

puzzles.title: Shrink strips playground
puzzles.controls: A row grows by turning every A into AB and every B into BA, all at once. Press Grow for the next row. Tap the top tile to start from the other letter.
rules: A row grows by turning every A into AB and every B into BA, all at once: A, AB, ABBA, ABBABAAB, and on. A piece is a run of tiles cut from a grown row.
Grow adds the next row, up to five rows. The top tile switches between A and B.
puzzles.idea: Free play with the growth rule: each row is the row before followed by the row before with A and B swapped.
puzzles.prerequisites: None beyond reading A and B.
hints: Before you grow the next row, say how it will start.
Each row starts with the whole row before it.
The second half of each row is the first half with A and B swapped.

parent.notice: Whether your child predicts the next row before pressing Grow, and whether they spot the row before inside the new one.
parent.prompt: What will the next row start with? How will it end?
parent.explanation: Each row is the row before with every A turned into AB and every B into BA, so it begins with the row before (A begins AB), and its second half is its first half with A and B swapped: A, AB, ABBA, ABBABAAB, ABBABAABBAABABBA. A grown row never has AAA or BBB, since it is made of pairs AB and BA.
parent.extension: Without growing, which letter is tile 11 of the row of 16? (Count from 0: tile 11 is number 10, 1010 in binary, with an even number of ones, so A.)
parent.connection: The Thue–Morse word: the tile numbered n (from 0) is A exactly when n has an even number of ones in binary. It turns up in Prouhet’s equal sums of powers, fair turn-taking and Thue’s overlap-free words.

puzzles.provenance: Week 76 Problem 1 (student page 1, Grades 3–5): grow a row of 16 tiles from A.

puzzles.title: Three short pieces
puzzles.objective: Keep every way to place seams on each piece from which it can shrink to one tile, then press That’s all.
puzzles.visibleObjective: Keep every way to place seams that lets a piece shrink to one tile.
puzzles.instruction: Keep every way to place seams on each piece from which it can shrink to one tile, then press That’s all.
puzzles.controls: A row grows by turning every A into AB and every B into BA, so a grown row splits into pairs AB and BA. Shrink undoes that: seams split a row into pairs, a tile cut off at an end gets its partner back (dashed, the other letter), and each pair becomes its first letter. A pair AA or BB is marked. puzzles.idea: A grown row is made of pairs AB and BA, so a way of placing seams that marks AA or BB is not how the piece was cut; a piece as short as ABA fits both ways.
puzzles.prerequisites: Read the letters A and B and see whether two letters are the same. No arithmetic. Following a row down through several shrinks takes patience; a grown-up can read How to play.
hints: Try both ways of placing seams on each piece, and shrink.
A way that marks AA or BB is stuck. ABA has no AA or BB either way.
Keep ABA both ways, BAABA paired from the first tile, and AABB with the first tile alone.

parent.notice: Whether your child shrinks before keeping a way or keeps it on sight, and whether they expect one way per piece.
parent.prompt: Where could ABA have been cut from? Can you find it in ABBABAABBAABABBA?
parent.explanation: A piece of a grown row has its seams either just before its first tile or one tile in. ABA fits both ways: paired from the first tile it is AB|A(B), which shrinks to AA, and with the first tile alone it is (B)A|BA, which shrinks to BB; each goes on to one tile (AA, BA, B and BB, AB, A). In ABBABAABBAABABBA it sits at tiles 4–6 and 11–13, once each way. BAABA fits only paired from the first tile: BA|AB|A(B) shrinks to BAA, then BA and B, while the other way marks AA. AABB fits only with the first tile alone: (B)A|AB|B(A) shrinks to BAB, then BB, AB and A. Four ways in all.
parent.extension: Which other pieces of three tiles fit both ways? (Only BAB.) Can a piece of four tiles?
parent.connection: The Thue–Morse word is the fixed point of the substitution A → AB, B → BA. Shrinking is desubstitution; pieces of four tiles or more can be cut into pairs in only one way, the word’s recognizability.

puzzles.idea: ABABA is in no grown row: it shrinks to AAA one way and BBB the other, and both mark a pair. So a strip repeating AB is an impostor.
puzzles.prerequisites: Read A and B and keep several rows in view. Choosing which tiles to test is the puzzle; the rows below are built one tap at a time.
hints: Choose a few tiles and shrink them. Does every way get stuck?
Runs of four tiles or fewer all shrink to one tile. Try five.
Choose tiles 1 to 5, ABABA. Paired from the first tile it shrinks to AAA, with the first tile alone to BBB, and both mark a pair.

parent.notice: Whether your child tries one way of placing seams and stops, or checks both ways before calling a row stuck.
parent.prompt: Could a grown row have ABABA in it? Where would its seams go?
parent.explanation: ABABA paired from the first tile is AB|AB|A(B) and shrinks to AAA; with the first tile alone it is (B)A|BA|BA and shrinks to BBB. AAA and BBB mark a pair both ways, so ABABA is stuck: no grown row has it, and a strip repeating AB is not cut from one. Shorter runs are not enough: AB, BA, ABA, BAB, ABAB and BABA all shrink to one tile, though ABAB only when paired from the first tile (the other way gives BBB).
parent.extension: Why can’t AAA or BBB sit in a grown row? (Any three neighbours include a whole pair.)
parent.connection: ABABA is an overlap: AB twice and then A again. Thue proved in 1912 that the Thue–Morse word has no overlaps at all.

puzzles.provenance: Week 76 Problem 6 (student page 4, Grades 3–5): the strip that repeats AB forever, “find a finite piece that cannot occur in any row grown from A”.

puzzles.idea: Three equal tiles never sit in a grown row, so the flipped tile is in BBB; only one of its three tiles fixes the piece.
puzzles.prerequisites: Read A and B, try a flip, shrink, and try another. Spotting AAA or BBB saves work.
hints: Shrink the piece as it is. Then try a flip and shrink again.
BBB can’t be in a grown row. Which of its tiles would you flip?
Flip tile 5 and keep it: AABBAABA shrinks to BABAA, BBA, AB and A. Flipping tile 3 or 4 leaves the piece stuck.

parent.notice: Whether your child flips a tile of BBB at once, and whether they see that the middle B makes a new problem.
parent.prompt: There are three B’s together. Which one would you change, and why does it matter which?
parent.explanation: A grown row is made of pairs AB and BA, so it never has three equal tiles in a row. AABBBABA has BBB at tiles 3–5, so the flipped tile is one of those. Flipping tile 3 gives AAABBABA, with AAA. Flipping tile 4 gives AABABABA, which hides ABABA, stuck both ways. Flipping tile 5 gives AABBAABA: with the first tile alone it is (B)A|AB|BA|AB|A(B), which shrinks to BABAA, then BBA, AB and A. A flip anywhere else leaves BBB, so tile 5 is the one fix.
parent.extension: Flip one tile of the grown row ABBABAAB and give it to a partner. Do they always find your tile, and only your tile?
parent.connection: A single wrong letter in a piece of the Thue–Morse word usually makes a short stuck run next to it, which narrows down where it is.

puzzles.provenance: New instance on Week 76 Problems 3–4: a piece of a grown row (AABBAABA) with one tile flipped, as the review card’s Decision asks.

puzzles.idea: A way with no marked pair can still be stuck lower down: ABAB with the first tile alone shrinks to BBB.
puzzles.prerequisites: Read the letters A and B and see whether two letters are the same. No arithmetic. Following a row down through several shrinks takes patience; a grown-up can read How to play.
hints: Before you keep a way, shrink it to one tile.
ABAB with the first tile alone shrinks to BBB. What happens to BBB?
Keep ABAB paired from the first tile, BAB both ways, and ABBAABBA paired from the first tile.

parent.notice: Whether your child keeps ABAB with the first tile alone because its top row has no AA or BB.
parent.prompt: This way has no marked pair. Is that enough?
parent.explanation: ABAB paired from the first tile is AB|AB, which shrinks to AA and on to one tile (AA, BA, B). With the first tile alone it is (B)A|BA|B(A), which shrinks to BBB, and BBB marks a pair both ways: stuck. BAB fits both ways (BA|B(A) shrinks to BB, (A)B|AB to AA). ABBAABBA paired from the first tile shrinks to ABAB, then AA, BA and B; with the first tile alone it marks BB. Four ways.
parent.extension: Worksheet Problem 5: can a piece of five tiles fit both ways?
parent.connection: Recognizability: a long enough piece of the Thue–Morse word has only one way to be cut into pairs (from four tiles on), while ABA and BAB have two.

puzzles.provenance: Week 76 Problem 4 (student page 3, Grades 3–5): the piece ABBAABBA, with ABAB and BAB added (new) for a way that is stuck one row down.

puzzles.idea: Shrinking a strip that repeats ABBA gives the strip that repeats AB, so the tiles that shrink to ABABA are stuck.
puzzles.prerequisites: Read A and B and keep several rows in view. Choosing which tiles to test is the puzzle; the rows below are built one tap at a time.
hints: Shrink a long run. What strip do the shrunk rows come from?
ABBA repeated shrinks to AB repeated, and ABABA is stuck. Which tiles shrink to ABABA?
Choose tiles 2 to 9, BBAABBAA. With the first tile alone it shrinks to ABABA; paired from the first tile it marks BB.

parent.notice: Whether your child recognizes the shrunk row ABAB… from the strip that repeats AB, and uses it to choose tiles.
parent.prompt: What does this strip shrink to? Have you seen that strip before?
parent.explanation: ABBA repeated, paired from the first tile, is AB|BA|AB|BA…, which shrinks to ABAB…, and that strip has ABABA, which is stuck. So tiles that shrink to ABABA are stuck too: ABBAABBAAB (ten tiles) paired from the first tile, or with the ghosts doing the ends, eight tiles: BBAABBAA, which with the first tile alone is (A)B|BA|AB|BA|A(B) and shrinks to ABABA, while paired from the first tile it marks BB. AABBAABB, from tile 4, shrinks to BABAB and marks AA the other way. No run of seven tiles or fewer is stuck.
parent.extension: Which is the shortest stuck run of a strip that repeats ABBABAAB? (Puzzle 10.)
parent.connection: Shrinking halves a repeating strip’s block (ABBA to AB). A grown row has no overlap, so any strip that repeats a block has a stuck run of at most two blocks and one tile (here ABBAABBAA).

puzzles.provenance: Week 76 Problem 6 (student page 4, Grades 3–5): the strip that repeats ABBA forever.

puzzles.idea: One flipped tile can have more than one repair: three different flips each give a piece of a grown row.
puzzles.prerequisites: Read A and B, try a flip, shrink, and try another. Spotting AAA or BBB saves work.
hints: Shrink the piece both ways. Which tiles are in a marked pair?
Paired from the first tile, BB at tiles 5 and 6 is marked; with the first tile alone, BB at tiles 2 and 3. A fix flips one of these.
Keep the flips of tiles 2, 5 and 6.

parent.notice: Whether your child stops at the first fix, perhaps ABBABAAB, which is a whole grown row.
parent.prompt: You found one fix. Could a different tile have been the flipped one?
parent.explanation: ABBABBAB is stuck: paired from the first tile it marks BB at tiles 5–6, and with the first tile alone BB at tiles 2–3. A flip elsewhere leaves both marks, so a fix flips one of tiles 2, 3, 5 and 6. Tile 6 gives ABBABAAB, the grown row itself. Tile 5 gives ABBAABAB, which shrinks to ABAA, then BBA, AB and A. Tile 2 gives AABABBAB, which with the first tile alone shrinks to BAABB, then BAB, BB, AB and A. Tile 3 gives ABAABBAB, whose unmarked way shrinks to BBABB, stuck. Three fixes.
parent.extension: Make a piece of eight tiles with one flipped tile and exactly two fixes.
parent.connection: An error in a piece of the Thue–Morse word can be detected without being located: several one-letter changes return to the word’s pieces.

parent.prompt: Where along the strip does it stop looking like a grown row?
parent.explanation: The strip is tiles 3 to 18 of the grown row ABBABAABBAABABBABAAB… with its 13th tile flipped from B to A. Tiles 9–13, ABABA, shrink to AAA one way and BBB the other, both stuck. puzzles.idea: Every short run of this strip fits a grown row; the impostor needs eight tiles, and it fails one row down, where AABAA marks a pair both ways.
puzzles.prerequisites: Read A and B and keep several rows in view. Choosing which tiles to test is the puzzle; the rows below are built one tap at a time.
hints: Choose a long run and shrink it. If it fits, slide the run along.
Runs of seven tiles or fewer all shrink to one tile.
Choose tiles 3 to 10, BABBAABA: paired from the first tile it marks BB, and with the first tile alone it shrinks to AABAA, which marks AA both ways.

parent.notice: Whether your child keeps choosing runs from the start of the strip, and whether shifting a run by a tile or two changes the result.
parent.prompt: This run shrinks fine. What if it starts one tile later?
parent.explanation: Every run of up to seven tiles of AABABB repeated sits in some grown row. BABBAABA (tiles 3–10, and again from tile 9) is stuck: paired from the first tile it marks BB; with the first tile alone it is (A)B|AB|BA|AB|A(B) and shrinks to AABAA, which marks AA paired from the first tile and, as (B)A|AB|AA, with the first tile alone too. The two nine-tile runs that contain it are stuck; every other run of nine tiles or fewer shrinks to one tile.
parent.extension: Why must a long enough run of any repeating strip be stuck? (Two blocks and one tile more make an overlap.)
parent.connection: Thue’s overlap-freeness: a strip that repeats a block u has the overlap uua, which no grown row contains; here a shorter run already fails.

puzzles.provenance: New instance on Week 76 Problem 6: a repeating strip whose short runs all fit.

Flipping a tile in the middle makes AAA or BBB.
Keep the flips of tile 1 and tile 8.

parent.notice: Whether your child rules out the middle tiles by spotting AAA or BBB, and then tries both ends.
parent.prompt: Which tiles can you rule out without shrinking?
parent.explanation: AABBAABB is stuck: paired from the first tile it marks AA, and with the first tile alone it shrinks to BABAB, which is stuck. Flipping any of tiles 2 to 7 makes AAA or BBB. Flipping tile 1 gives BABBAABB, which with the first tile alone shrinks to AABAB, then BAA, BA and B. Flipping tile 8 gives AABBAABA, which shrinks to BABAA, then BBA, AB and A. Two fixes, one at each end: the piece alone can’t tell which end was wrong.
parent.extension: Find a piece with one flipped tile whose only fix is in the middle. (Puzzle 3 is one.)
parent.connection: Locating an error needs room on both sides of it: near the ends of a piece the evidence can point two ways.

puzzles.idea: A grown row repeated forever is not a grown row: shrinking three times reaches ABABA.
puzzles.prerequisites: Read A and B and keep several rows in view. Choosing which tiles to test is the puzzle; the rows below are built one tap at a time.
hints: Shrink a long run. What strip do the shrunk rows come from?
ABBABAAB repeated shrinks to ABBA repeated, and then to AB repeated. Which tiles shrink to ABABA?
Choose tiles 4 to 17, ABAABABBABAABA: with the first tile alone it shrinks to BBAABBAA, then ABABA, which is stuck both ways.

parent.notice: Whether your child uses the earlier repeating strips: this one shrinks to ABBA repeated and then to AB repeated.
parent.prompt: What does this strip shrink to? And that one?
parent.explanation: ABBABAAB repeated, paired from the first tile, shrinks to ABBA repeated and then to AB repeated, which has ABABA. Tracing ABABA back up gives ABAABABBABAABA (tiles 4–17, and again from tile 8): paired from the first tile it marks AA; with the first tile alone it shrinks to BBAABBAA, which marks BB one way and shrinks to ABABA the other, and ABABA shrinks to AAA or BBB. No run of thirteen tiles or fewer is stuck.
parent.extension: Two copies, ABBABAABABBABAAB, do sit in a grown row (worksheet Problem 3 asks whether it is a whole one). Where?
parent.connection: Squares such as ABBABAABABBABAAB occur in the Thue–Morse word, but overlaps do not (Thue, 1912), so three copies of a block never do.
